description: Committee recommends regulating new building energy standards to Tier 2.
Tier 2 improves energy performance 10%, saving $300 annually.
This aligns with city's Low Emissions Community plan.

chips.text: Recommended to Council
6 for, 0 against
Home builders' CEO reported members are split, with 60-70% supporting Tier 1 and 30-40% Tier 2.
Builders face higher upfront costs and potential delays from blower door tests.
Home Builders' Association raised concerns about costs, affordability, and inconsistent regulations.
Affordability concerns raised for builders focused on delivering attainable housing.
Tier 2 aligns with the city's goal of net-zero new home construction by 2036.

speakers.name: Nicole Burgess
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: Energy Regulation Options for Building Standards
said: Many builders voluntarily met Tier 2 before it was required.
Tier 2 adds costs and delays from required blower door tests.
Builders need certainty, collaboration, and a level playing field.

segments.title: Administration introduces energy regulation options
segments.takeaway: Administration introduces the report on energy regulation options for building standards, detailing implications, benefits, and stakeholder preferences for Tier 1 or Tier 2.

segments.title: Homebuilders Association presents concerns
segments.takeaway: Nicole Burgess from the Homebuilders Association presents industry concerns about regulation timing, varying standards across municipalities, and the impact of additional costs on housing affordabilit

segments.title: Environmental Society advocates for Tier 2
segments.takeaway: Peter Prebble from the Saskatchewan Environmental Society urges the committee to support Tier 2, citing environmental benefits, long-term homeowner savings, and alignment with climate goals.

segments.title: Committee questions administration
segments.takeaway: Committee members question administration about the current reversion to Tier 1, the impacts on the Low Emissions Community Plan, and the process for re-implementing Tier 2.

segments.title: Committee votes on energy regulation
segments.takeaway: The committee votes to approve administration's recommendation to regulate building energy standards to Tier 2, aligning with the city's low emissions community plan.

description: Recommends continuing enhanced enforcement for vacant, boarded buildings.
Recommends approving amendments to Property Maintenance Bylaw.

chips.text: Recommended to Council
6 for, 0 against
Councillor Timon moved to explore tax tools for long-term vacant properties.
Saskatoon Fire Department tracks 68 active vacant and boarded building files.

segments.title: Saskatoon Fire Department Report on Boarded Buildings
segments.takeaway: The Saskatoon Fire Department reported on its initiatives to address vacant and boarded properties, highlighting a reduction from 280 to 68 active files since 2020.

segments.title: Questions on Boarded Buildings Report
segments.takeaway: Councillors questioned legislative limitations for implementing tools similar to other cities and inquired about the trend of complaints regarding boarded buildings since 2018.

segments.title: Decision on Boarded Buildings and New Motion
segments.takeaway: The committee approved the recommendations and a motion directing administration to explore property tax surplus or other fiscal tools to discourage long-term vacancies.

description: Saskatoon could reallocate $4M to affordable housing calls.
New brownfield and refocused VLAR incentives are proposed.
These changes aim to boost Saskatoon's housing supply.

chips.text: Recommended to Council
6 for, 0 against
Mayor Block found the report complex, wished for more pre-committee discussion.
Affordable units must be below SHIMS and cost under 30% of income.
New brownfield incentive supports environmental reports and remediation.
Administration will release new affordable housing call by June.

segments.title: Housing Accelerator Fund Background and Targets
segments.takeaway: Staff presented background on the federal Housing Accelerator Fund, its targets for housing supply, and how they align with the city's growth goals and Official Community Plan.

segments.title: HAF Incentives and Proposed Reallocation
segments.takeaway: Administration proposed reallocating up to $4 million from the existing HAF rebate program to fund an additional call for affordable housing units, while discontinuing the rebate program.

segments.title: Proposed Changes to VLAR Program
segments.takeaway: Administration proposed refocusing the Vacant Lot and Adaptive Reuse (VLAR) program to support development in priority growth areas and discontinuing its current form by December 2025.

segments.title: Proposed New Brownfield Incentive
segments.takeaway: Administration proposed a new financial incentive program, initially funded by HAF, to support environmental reports and remediation efforts on brownfield sites in priority growth areas.

segments.title: Summary of Proposed Actions and Next Steps
segments.takeaway: Administration summarized the upcoming incentive programs, the additional call for affordable housing, and the development of new policies for VLAR and Brownfield incentives, requesting direction to p

segments.title: Committee Questions and Staff Clarifications
segments.takeaway: Committee members asked staff questions regarding the reallocation of funds, missing middle targets, the definition of affordable housing, and criteria for unit sizes in new proposals.

segments.title: Motion and Vote on Recommendations
segments.takeaway: The committee moved and carried the recommendations from the report, providing direction for administration to proceed with the proposed incentive approaches.

description: Committee recommends $1.07 million in 2025 tax abatements.

chips.text: Recommended to Council
6 for, 0 against
Six recreation, 18 social services, and six culture groups benefit.
Persephone Theatre provides $60,000 annually in free or subsidized space.
AK Artist Run Center prioritizes serving equity-deserving communities.

speakers.name: Breanne Harmon
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: Persephone Theare - 2025 Cultural Grant Capital Reserve Awards
said: Persephone Theatre is a cornerstone of Saskatoon's cultural landscape.
It champions local talent and serves the community through various programs.
Tax abatement is integral to its success and Saskatoon's world-class status.

segments.title: Administration report on tax abatements
segments.takeaway: The administration presented a report recommending approval of $331,335 in tax abatements for 30 eligible organizations across three programs, funded through the 2025 operating budget.

segments.title: Persephone Theatre presentation
segments.takeaway: Brian Harmon from Persephone Theatre highlighted the theatre's 50-year history, community engagement, and economic impact, emphasizing the tax abatement program's importance to its success.

segments.title: AK Artist Run Center presentation
segments.takeaway: Terran Deod from AK Artist Run Center explained how the tax abatement program enables them to serve equity-deserving communities and operate as a thriving arts hub.

segments.title: Motion to approve tax abatements
segments.takeaway: Councillor Block moved to approve the recommended tax abatements for the eligible organizations, acknowledging the value of the presentations.
